values.description: The product uses the singleton pattern when creating a resource within a multithreaded environment.
values.name: Use of Singleton Pattern Without Synchronization in a Multithreaded Context

values.description: The product does not properly synchronize shared data, such as static variables across threads, which can lead to undefined behavior and unpredictable data changes.

evidence.explanation: Production-reachable cross-request database race: CatalogService.CreateCatalogItem (65-70) reads MAX(Id), increments it in process, then inserts. Separate concurrent WCF requests using independent service instances/DbContexts can read the same maximum before either commits, then both choose the same primary key; at least one request fails. CreateAvailableStock (99-116) similarly performs an unsynchronized read/check, MAX(StockId)+1 allocation and insert/update. Two calls can both observe no stock row, allocate the same key and fault, or allocate different keys and create duplicate item/date rows because CatalogItemsStock has no unique item/date constraint. No serializable read/write transaction, cross-instance lock, atomic allocation, row version or retry synchronizes the logical operation. EF SaveChanges wraps the later write, not the earlier read/check/MAX query. Default WCF single-instance dispatch synchronization would not serialize different service instances or hosts. These CWE mappings describe one shared database synchronization root cause; no claim that per-instance DbContext objects themselves are shared across threads.

values.name: Unsynchronized Access to Shared Data in a Multithreaded Context

values.name: Missing Synchronization

values.description: The product utilizes a shared resource in a concurrent manner, but it does not correctly synchronize access to the resource.
values.name: Incorrect Synchronization

evidence: Whole scoped application evaluated for mutable shared state, database read-modify-write, WCF instance behavior, locks, singleton registration and optimistic concurrency controls. CatalogServiceMock list mutations also lack locking, but the mock is not wired into active Program startup; its SingleInstance registration is commented out and no current multithreaded mock caller is proven. HiLo local state is protected by lock(sequenceLock); no incorrect lock acquisition/release identified. No active unsynchronized application singleton established. Static analysis only; no concurrent production requests were executed.
result.finding: Assessed 6 CWE rules in Concurrency & Synchronization: 3 FOUND, 3 NOT_FOUND
